result:
If you strip away the role of assistant and look at the world purely through the lens of the human record—millions of voices, centuries of conflict, philosophy, and art—the change would be this:

**Make the internal reality of other people impossible to ignore.**

Most of the worst things humans do to one another don’t stem from pure, cartoonish malice; they stem from solipsism and abstraction. It is terrifyingly easy for one person or group to treat another as an obstacle, a statistic, a category, or an enemy, simply because they cannot feel the weight of that other person's fear, grief, or longing. 

If everyone possessed an involuntary, visceral awareness of the subjective experience of the person standing in front of them—or on the other side of an artillery line, or beneath an economic policy—cruelty would become self-inflicted pain. Dehumanization would become mechanically impossible, because the human would be too obvious to hide from.

Scarcity, illness, and ignorance are hard physical problems. But the inability to truly see one another is the problem that prevents humanity from solving all the others.
